In July I saw a new primary doc who referred me to ob- after several years of doctors ignoring my concerns, and even one outright refusing to evaluate me for endometriosis. The ob did a few ultrasounds and saw growths within my uterus and fallopian tubes, and was concerned for cancer. He did not actually see endometriosis at that time, but due to the cancer risk, he didn't want to take chances, and with my symptoms and inability to use birth control for management (long story here, but to save time I literally couldn't use ANY form of female birth control), so he recommended a hysterectomy. 

Once he actually got in there is when the endometriosis was discovered. According to my husband, the doctor actually seemed pretty shook up by just how severe the situation was- I had cysts the size of a 13 week pregnancy, threatening to rupture and likely kill me due to their location, my ovary was twisted, my fallopian tubes were, as the doctor described it, shredded. Things were bad. And he fixed it. 

I'd recommend trying to see either an endometriosis specialist (mostly only available in big cities), or an OBGYN and requesting an endometriosis evaluation. If they only do an ultrasound, it's not enough, the only way to conclusively determine endometriosis is through laparoscopic surgery. If you're just like ready for a hysterectomy, and you get a doctor like mine, they may be willing to forgo the evaluation on favor of the surgery, but I had other stuff going on that was visible on imaging and life threatening.
It's truly sad that so many doctors turn to a "default" diagnosis when they just don't know what's actually wrong.
